subject: Subprocessor decomposition & dataflow mapping for SOC2/CAIQ audit — Redwood integration
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@databridge.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: subprocessor decomposition and dataflow map for SOC2 audit — Redwood integration

Hi Neha,

We're kicking off the SOC2 evidence collection for the joint integration between DataBridge and Redwood. Our auditor has asked for: a) a flat subprocessor decomposition for any third parties that process customer data as part of the integration (including analytics, backups, logging, CDN, observability), b) a high-level dataflow diagram showing where customer PII/derived model outputs transit and are stored, and c) any attestation references (SOC/ISO) you can provide for those subprocessors.

Can you provide a CSV or similar that includes vendor name, purpose, data types (e.g., customer prompts, logs, metrics), access level (read/write), and retention window? We have a preliminary deadline of 2026-08-19 for evidence to bundle into the auditor portal.

Also please call out any vendors that have cross-border transfers or that maintain backups in different regions. If you have an existing CAIQ/SIG mapping for this integration that would speed things up.

Thanks — if it's easier to send incrementally that's fine.

Regards,
Sarah Liu
Security Program Manager
DataBridge Security

--
Attachment: audit-request-initial.pdf (application/pdf, stub)

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching an initial package (see attachment list below) and a short summary here. We can expand any row in the CSV with additional evidence (eg. attestation links).

Short summary:
- Subprocessor inventory attached (subprocessor_inventory_20260810.csv). Contains vendor, purpose, data elements, access level, region, retention.
- Dataflow diagram attached (redwood-dataflow-diagram-20260810.pdf). High level shows integration points: ingestion -> inference runtime -> ephemeral KV cache -> observability pipelines -> backups.
- Major items to flag: our analytics vendor (PulseStats) sees aggregated telemetry only; our object storage provider (S3-managed by AlphaCloud) hosts customer backups and model cache snapshots and is configured with restricted IAM roles.

Next steps: Rishi (cc'd) will confirm retention windows for logs and backups, Marissa will attach attestation index (SOC2/ISO links). We can provide an expanded access matrix for S3 buckets by 2026-08-13 per your deadline.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20260810.csv, redwood-dataflow-diagram-20260810.pdf

Thanks — this is helpful. Auditor follow-up: can you provide more granularity on S3/object-store access? They want a column that shows which subprocessors have read vs write vs admin privileges per bucket (e.g., backups-bucket-prod, cache-snapshots-us-west). Also need confirmation of cross-border copy behavior (do backups replicate to other regions?).

Second, we're collecting attestation references (PDF links) for any subprocessor with an external SOC2 Type II or ISO certificate. Can Marissa surface an index file that maps vendor -> attestation link and scope?

Finally — deadline is firm for evidence ingestion: 2026-08-19 COB. If you foresee issues with the bucket-level matrix, call that out and we'll accept a targeted interim deliverable by 2026-08-15 with final by the 19th.

Appreciate it,
Sarah

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@databridge.com>

Date: 2026-08-13T17:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor decomposition and dataflow map for SOC2 audit — Redwood integration

Sarah — attaching the expanded deliverable per your follow-ups. Summary of what's included below and next steps.

What we attached:
- s3-access-matrix-20260813.xlsx: per-bucket access (read/write/admin) for named vendors and internal service accounts. Buckets spelled out: backups-bucket-prod (us-west-2), cache-snapshots-us-west, logs-central-eu (replicated from us-west for EU customers).
- SOC2-attestations-index.txt: vendor -> attestation link and scope (PulseStats: SOC2 Type II - telemetry only; AlphaCloud Storage: SOC2 Type II + ISO27001; CDNCo: SOC2 Type II for edge caching).
- NOTE: backup replication — AlphaCloud configuration replicates backups to us-west-2 and us-east-1 by default for DR; no copies are retained in EU unless customer opts into EU-region-only retention (we document region isolation per customer account).

A few operational notes:
- Access is role-based. We use short-lived IAM credentials for service accounts and S3 presigned URLs where possible. Admin-level access is strictly limited to our infra team and AlphaCloud's managed-maintenance role (audited monthly).
- Retention windows: backups: 30/90/365 configurable by customer — default is 90 days for integration customers; logs and observability traces: 90 days (aggregated/pseudonymized).
- For any vendor where you need the raw attestation PDF, Marissa will upload direct copies to the drive link and include the auditor bundle.

Deliverable timeline:
- Interim: s3-access-matrix and attestation index delivered with this email (see attachments).
- Final: expanded evidence bundle (full attestation PDFs, STIG/CAIQ mapping excerpt) to the Drive folder by 2026-08-16. If you need the full CSV exported to HubSpot/portal earlier, tell us preferred format.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-subprocessors-2026 (attestations and full PDF set will be added)

If anything is missing, ping me and we'll prioritize.

Best,
